text:
Ancient Egypt was a fascinating civilization that thrived along the Nile River thousands of years ago. The Egyptians are famous for building massive stone structures called pyramids, which served as grand tombs for their rulers, known as pharaohs. These pharaohs held power similar to modern-day kings or queens and were believed to have divine connections. The pyramids were not only impressive feats of engineering but also reflected the Egyptians' deep beliefs about life, death, and the afterlife.

Name the tool used for writing:

The primary tool used for writing in Ancient Egypt was a reed pen. Scribes dipped these reed pens into ink made from soot, water, and other natural materials to write on papyrus, which was a type of paper made from the papyrus plant.
